raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
- `amd_ci_fault_trap.c`: a SIGSEGV, SIGBUS and SIGABRT handler that prints the native backtrace, naming the library that faulted, and then lets the fault proceed as before
- `amd_ci_fast_exit.py`: load it underneath Python's faulthandler, so a fault prints the Python traceback and then the native one; an image without the library runs as before, with a one-line warning
- `Dockerfile.rocm`: build the library into the test image (one `cc` call, cached unless the source changes)
- `test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py`, CI configs: tests for the report and for a missing library, run when the `.c` file changes

When an AMD CI job crashes in native code, Python's faulthandler shows only the Python frames, so the log does not say whether the fault came from HIP, the ROCm runtime, Ray or a vLLM extension; now every native fault in a pytest run also prints the native frames, while the job's result stays exactly what it was. This PR first also turned a fault after pytest's summary into pytest's own exit status, because of [vllm/ci #96786](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96786), where every test passed and the process then died in interpreter teardown. #61939's fast exit now skips that teardown, no fault after the summary shows up in the AMD builds that ran with it ([15532](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15532), [15739](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15739)), and the mapping would also have turned a teardown SIGABRT green, so that part is dropped. The plugin keeps its name, so this does not conflict with #64132, which changes how the same plugin is installed. Follow-up to #61939; `pytest tests/tools/test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py` passes 11 tests (3 new) in 10 runs out of 10, and the library has not been built in AMD CI yet.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

detail.title: [ROCm][CI] Print the native backtrace of a fault in AMD CI pytest runs

files.patch:
@@ -12,14 +12,26 @@
 
 Off when a kernel recorder is loaded (it writes its trace during native teardown)
 or with VLLM_CI_FAST_EXIT=0.
+
+It also loads a native fault reporter (amd_ci_fault_trap.c, built into the CI image):
+a SIGSEGV, SIGBUS or SIGABRT prints the native backtrace, which names the library that
+faulted, after Python's traceback. VLLM_CI_FAULT_TRAP_LIB overrides the library's path.
 """
 
 import atexit
+import ctypes
+import faulthandler
 import os
 import sys
 
 import pytest
 
+_LIB = os.environ.get(
+    "VLLM_CI_FAULT_TRAP_LIB", "/usr/local/lib/libamd_ci_fault_trap.so"
+)
+# The real stderr, taken before pytest captures fd 2, so a fault report is never
+# swallowed by a test's captured output.
+_stderr_fd = os.dup(2)
 _outer = None
 _session = None
 
@@ -32,10 +44,32 @@ def _recorder_loaded() -> bool:
     )
 
 
+def _install_fault_reporter(lib) -> None:
+    # Python's faulthandler restores the handler it replaced when it is disabled, so
+    # take its place underneath it: it prints the Python traceback, then hands the
+    # fault on.
+    python_handler = faulthandler.is_enabled()
+    if python_handler:
+        faulthandler.disable()
+    if lib.amd_ci_trap_install(_stderr_fd):
+        os.write(_stderr_fd, b"[amd-ci] could not install the native fault reporter\n")
+    if python_handler:
+        faulthandler.enable(file=_stderr_fd)
+
+
+@pytest.hookimpl(trylast=True)  # after pytest's faulthandler plugin has enabled it
 def pytest_configure(config):
     global _outer
-    if _outer is None:  # pytester runs nested sessions in-process; act on the outer one
-        _outer = config
+    if _outer is not None:  # pytester runs nested sessions in-process: act on the outer
+        return
+    _outer = config
+    try:
+        lib = ctypes.CDLL(_LIB)
+    except OSError as exc:  # an image without it: run the tests without the reporter
+        os.write(_stderr_fd, f"[amd-ci] no native fault reporter: {exc}\n".encode())
+        return
+    lib.amd_ci_trap_install.argtypes = [ctypes.c_int]
+    _install_fault_reporter(lib)
 
 
 def pytest_sessionfinish(session, exitstatus):

@@ -132,6 +132,7 @@ steps:
   - tests/tools/test_rocm_build.py
   - tests/tools/test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py
   - .buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/amd_ci_fast_exit.py
+  - .buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/amd_ci_fault_trap.c
   - tests/tools/test_kernel_symbol_map.py
   - tools/ci/kernel_symbol_map.py
   - tools/ci/rocm_kernel_symbol_map.py

@@ -22,6 +22,7 @@ steps:
     - tests/tools/test_rocm_build.py
     - tests/tools/test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py
     - .buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/amd_ci_fast_exit.py
+    - .buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/amd_ci_fault_trap.c
     - tests/tools/test_kernel_symbol_map.py
     - tools/ci/kernel_symbol_map.py
     - tools/ci/rocm_kernel_symbol_map.py
@@ -49,6 +50,7 @@ steps:
       - tests/tools/test_rocm_build.py
       - tests/tools/test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py
       - .buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/amd_ci_fast_exit.py
+      - .buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/amd_ci_fault_trap.c
       - tests/tools/test_kernel_symbol_map.py
       - tools/ci/kernel_symbol_map.py
       - tools/ci/rocm_kernel_symbol_map.py

@@ -554,6 +554,9 @@ RUN --mount=type=bind,source=.buildkite/scripts/rocm/select_aiter_nightly_wheel.
     fi
 
 FROM test-base AS test
+# Native fault reporter for AMD CI pytest runs (.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/amd_ci_fast_exit.py).
+RUN --mount=type=bind,source=.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/amd_ci_fault_trap.c,target=/tmp/trap.c \
+    cc -O2 -shared -fPIC -o /usr/local/lib/libamd_ci_fault_trap.so /tmp/trap.c
 COPY --link --from=native /out /
 COPY --link --from=install /out /
 COPY --link --exclude=vllm --exclude=.git . /vllm-workspace/

@@ -1,8 +1,11 @@
 # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
-"""The AMD CI pytest plugin skips native teardown without changing pytest's result."""
+"""The AMD CI pytest plugin skips native teardown without changing pytest's result,
+and reports native faults."""
 
 import os
+import shlex
+import shutil
 import signal
 import subprocess
 import sys
@@ -11,6 +14,7 @@
 import pytest
 
 PLUGIN_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / ".buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci"
+IMAGE_LIB = Path("/usr/local/lib/libamd_ci_fault_trap.so")
 
 # An object that segfaults when the interpreter tears its module down, after the
 # summary, as native library destructors did in vllm/ci #96786.
@@ -102,3 +106,42 @@ def test_a_nested_in_process_session_does_not_end_the_outer_one(tmp_path):
     result = _run(tmp_path, body)
     assert result.returncode == 0, result.stdout + result.stderr
     assert "2 passed" in result.stdout
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def reporter(tmp_path_factory):
+    """The image's fault reporter library, else one built from source."""
+    if IMAGE_LIB.exists():
+        return {"VLLM_CI_FAULT_TRAP_LIB": str(IMAGE_LIB)}
+    cc = os.environ.get("CC") or shutil.which("cc") or shutil.which("gcc")
+    if not cc:
+        pytest.skip("no fault reporter library and no compiler to build one")
+    lib = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("reporter") / "libamd_ci_fault_trap.so"
+    source = PLUGIN_DIR / "amd_ci_fault_trap.c"
+    subprocess.run(
+        [*shlex.split(cc), "-O2", "-shared", "-fPIC", "-o", str(lib), str(source)],
+        check=True,
+    )
+    return {"VLLM_CI_FAULT_TRAP_LIB": str(lib)}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "fault, sig",
+    [
+        ("__import__('ctypes').string_at(0)", signal.SIGSEGV),
+        ("__import__('os').abort()", signal.SIGABRT),
+    ],
+)
+def test_a_native_fault_is_reported_and_still_fails(tmp_path, reporter, fault, sig):
+    result = _run(tmp_path, f"\ndef test_fault():\n    {fault}\n", env=reporter)
+    assert result.returncode == -sig
+    # Python's traceback first, then the native one, which names the library.
+    python_tb = result.stderr.index("Fatal Python error")
+    assert result.stderr.index(f"native fault: {sig.name}") > python_tb
+    assert ".so" in result.stderr.split("native fault")[1]
+
+
+def test_without_the_library_the_tests_run_as_before(tmp_path):
+    result = _run(tmp_path, PASSING, env={"VLLM_CI_FAULT_TRAP_LIB": "/nonexistent.so"})
+    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
+    assert "no native fault reporter" in result.stderr
